title: Subarray Sums Divisible by K
statement: Count the non-empty subarrays of the integer array `nums` whose elements add up to a multiple of `k` (zero and negative multiples included), and return that count. A subarray is a run of consecutive elements; runs at different positions are counted separately even when their values are the same.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every pair of start and end costs O(n²). Instead, think of prefix sums: the sum of `nums[i..j]` is `P[j+1] - P[i]`, and that difference is a multiple of `k` exactly when the two prefix sums leave the same remainder modulo `k`. So every subarray we want corresponds to a pair of equal prefix remainders, and we only need to count, while scanning, how many earlier prefixes share the current remainder.

## Approach

1. Make the array `seen` of size `k`, where `seen[r]` counts prefixes with remainder `r`. The empty prefix has sum 0, so `seen[0] = 1`.
2. Scan `nums`, adding each `num` to `prefix` and reducing it to a remainder in `0..k-1` (adding `k` before the last `% k` fixes negative remainders).
3. Every earlier prefix with the same remainder starts a valid subarray ending here, so add `seen[prefix]` to `count`.
4. Record the current prefix by incrementing `seen[prefix]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [4,5,0,-2,-3,1]`, `k = 5`, `seen` starts as `{0: 1}`.

| num | prefix | seen[prefix] before | count |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| 5 | 4 | 1 | 1 |
| 0 | 4 | 2 | 3 |
| -2 | 2 | 0 | 3 |
| -3 | 4 | 3 | 6 |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | 7 |

The answer is `7`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + k): one pass over `nums`, plus creating `seen`.
- Space: O(k) for the remainder counts.

## Pitfalls

- In JavaScript (and Java, C) `-3 % 5` is `-3`, not `2`; normalise with `((x % k) + k) % k` or equal remainders will be missed.
- Forgetting `seen[0] = 1` drops every subarray that starts at index 0.
- Add `seen[prefix]` to the count **before** incrementing it, or each prefix pairs with itself as an empty subarray.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | `seen[r]` = how many prefixes so far have remainder `r` |
| `prefix` | remainder of the running sum modulo `k`, in `0..k-1` |
| `num` | the current element |
| `count` | number of divisible subarrays found so far |

narration.2: seen[r] will count how many prefix sums so far leave remainder r when divided by k.
narration.3: The empty prefix has sum 0, so remainder 0 has already been seen once.
narration.4: prefix holds the running sum, kept as a remainder modulo k.
narration.5: count accumulates the number of divisible subarrays.
narration.7: Extend the prefix by one element at a time.
narration.8: Add the element and reduce to a remainder in 0..k-1; adding k first fixes negative values.
narration.9: Each earlier prefix with this remainder starts a subarray ending here whose sum is a multiple of k.
narration.10: Record this prefix so later positions can pair with it.
narration.12: Return the total number of divisible subarrays.
